title: Driftward Plateau
description: An asymmetric faulted limestone island with a long keel, detached fragments and a grass-capped summit. The keel starts near Z=0.

review.notes: Rebuild, round 1 of the new budget. Good: a strong asymmetric silhouette with a long tapering keel, pale ivory limestone strata with vertical joints, an olive meadow with grouped trees, rocks and a path, a turf rim with hanging grass, and small satellite islands (hero, turn tiles). Still failing: (1) the bed undersides are flat, smooth beige plates with straight edges, so the keel reads as stacked trays or an inverted ziggurat; one chamfered face at the upper left of closeup_base is a flat untextured slab. (2) The keel ends in a thin needle spike (closeup_base). (3) A loose flat grey plate floats left of the keel in one turn tile (turn 4), and white flat wedges stick out of the underside in the neutral-material tile. (4) A pure black wedge sits on the far-left rim of the meadow (closeup_upper). (5) The cliff faces are soft, blotchy noise between the joints instead of crisp fracture planes, and the turf sheet sits on the rock with a dark seam and no soil or roots. Fix: break the ledge soffits into fractured, dripping undersides of varied depth, end the keel in a blunt broken tip with a few hanging roots, remove the stray plate, wedges and black rim object, give the faces sharper fracture planes with darker joints, and add a soil band with roots between turf and rock.
